common_name: Sleeping Giant Chestnut (Blight-Resistant Connecticut Complex Hybrid Chestnut)
scientific_name: Castanea mollissima x (crenata x dentata) 'Sleeping Giant'

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in early spring in deep, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun; needs a genetically distinct second chestnut tree nearby for cross-pollination and nut set.

directions: Sleeping Giant is a complex mollissima x (crenata x dentata) hybrid selected by Arthur H. Graves at the Sleeping Giant chestnut plantation in Hamden, Connecticut, part of the Connecticut Agricultural Experiment Station's early chestnut breeding program. It has recorded resistance to chestnut blight and produces medium-sized nuts, roughly 15 grams each, with excellent, sweet flavor and good pellicle (skin) removal, ripening from mid- to late September. Plant it with a second, genetically distinct chestnut cultivar nearby, since Sleeping Giant will not reliably set a crop on its own.

common_name: Layeroka Chestnut (Gellatly Pacific Northwest Hybrid Chestnut)

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; pollen-sterile and must be planted with a distinct pollinizer cultivar, such as Skioka, to produce a nut crop.

directions: Layeroka (Gellatly #1) is a European x Japanese chestnut hybrid selected by nurseryman J.U. Gellatly of Westbank, British Columbia, and it has become a mainstay of Pacific Northwest chestnut orchards for its productivity and cold hardiness rather than for strong blight resistance. It bears medium-sized, sweet nuts that drop free of the bur but do not store well, so plan to use or process the crop soon after the September harvest. Because Layeroka is pollen-sterile, it must be interplanted with a genetically distinct, overlapping-bloom pollinizer, growers commonly use the Gellatly selection Skioka for this purpose.

common_name: Skioka Chestnut (Gellatly Chinese Chestnut Pollinizer Selection)

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; prized as a heavy, reliable pollen source for pollen-sterile Pacific Northwest hybrids and also bears its own crop of nuts.

directions: Skioka (Gellatly #2) is an open-pollinated Chinese chestnut seedling selected by J.U. Gellatly in British Columbia and is grown chiefly as a dependable, heavy pollen producer rather than for its own nut crop. It is commonly interplanted with pollen-sterile Pacific Northwest hybrid selections, such as Layeroka, to ensure full pollination and a reliable nut set on those trees. Skioka itself also produces nuts and, as a Chinese chestnut seedling, benefits from the species' generally good resistance to chestnut blight.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; pollen-sterile and needs a compatible pollinizer cultivar nearby to set a nut crop.

directions: Skookum is a Gellatly-lineage hybrid chestnut selected by W. Schildgen and grown in Pacific Northwest orchards for its good nut flavor and regional adaptation. Blight resistance records for Skookum are mixed rather than fully resistant, so it is best sited where blight pressure is manageable or combined with other resistant cultivars in a planting. Because it is pollen-sterile, Skookum must be planted alongside a genetically distinct, overlapping-bloom pollinizer to produce nuts.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; grown mainly as a pollen source for other Pacific Northwest chestnut selections and also produces its own nut crop.

directions: Myoka is a Chinese chestnut seedling selection made by J.U. Gellatly in British Columbia and is valued in Pacific Northwest orchards primarily as a reliable pollinizer for other regional chestnut cultivars. As a Chinese chestnut selection it carries the species' generally good natural resistance to chestnut blight. Plant it alongside pollen-sterile hybrids such as Layeroka or Skookum to ensure a full nut set across the planting.

common_name: Douglas #1A Chestnut (Blight-Resistant Chinese Chestnut Hybrid Selection)

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; needs a genetically distinct second chestnut tree nearby for cross-pollination and nut set.

directions: Douglas #1A is a Chinese chestnut hybrid selected by breeder E. Douglas and carries recorded resistance to chestnut blight. Nuts are modest in size, around 8 grams, and ripen early, typically from the first to the third week of September, making it a useful early-season selection in a mixed chestnut planting. Like most chestnuts, it will not self-pollinate reliably and should be planted with a distinct, overlapping-bloom cultivar nearby.

common_name: Orrin Chestnut (Good Blight-Resistant Chinese Chestnut Selection)

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; needs a genetically distinct second chestnut tree nearby for cross-pollination and nut set.

directions: Orrin is a Chinese chestnut selection made by O.S. Good and carries recorded resistance to chestnut blight. It bears modest-sized nuts, around 8 grams, with good flavor, ripening from mid- to late September. Plant it with a genetically distinct second chestnut cultivar for reliable cross-pollination and a full nut set.

common_name: Fowler Chestnut (UC Davis Large-Nutted European Hybrid Selection)

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; pollen-sterile and must be planted with a distinct, overlapping-bloom pollinizer to set a nut crop.

directions: Fowler (UCD 92-359-1) is a European chestnut hybrid selected by K. Ryugo in the University of California, Davis chestnut breeding program and is notable for large nuts, roughly 22 to 25 grams each, with a thin pellicle that peels away easily. Nuts drop free of the bur without the internal shell-invagination problems that trouble some other large-nutted selections. Fowler is pollen-sterile, so it must be interplanted with a compatible, genetically distinct chestnut cultivar to produce a crop.

common_name: Szego Chestnut (Nave Large-Nutted Blight-Resistant Hybrid Chestnut)

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; needs a genetically distinct second chestnut tree nearby for cross-pollination and nut set.

directions: Szego is a hybrid chestnut selected by chestnut grower J. Michael Nave and carries recorded resistance to chestnut blight. It stands out for its unusually large, single-embryo nuts, around 40 grams each, and excellent flavor, and it is reported to graft readily onto a wide range of chestnut rootstocks. As with other chestnuts, plant it with a second, genetically distinct cultivar nearby to ensure reliable cross-pollination.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; needs a genetically distinct second chestnut tree nearby for cross-pollination and nut set.

directions: Simpson is a Chinese x European chestnut hybrid selected by W. Simpson and carries recorded resistance to chestnut blight. It produces good-flavored nuts around 11 grams each, though some nuts have multiple embryos, and it ripens later than many selections, from late September into early October. Plant it with a genetically distinct second chestnut cultivar for reliable cross-pollination and a full nut set.

common_name: Benton Harbor Chestnut (Michigan State University Chinese Chestnut Selection)

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; needs a genetically distinct second chestnut tree nearby for cross-pollination and nut set.

directions: Benton Harbor is a Chinese chestnut seedling selection from Michigan State University's Benton Harbor, Michigan research station, valued for its cold hardiness and high, dependable yields, growers in Michigan have reported 70 to 90 pounds of nuts per mature tree. It produces dark red-purple nuts that peel well and are largely free of the double embryos and splits that reduce quality in some other selections, and it tends to bear earlier in the season than many Chinese chestnut selections. Field observations note good resistance to chestnut blight, though performance can vary by site. Plant with a genetically distinct second chestnut cultivar for reliable cross-pollination.

common_name: Belle Epine Chestnut (French Late-Ripening European Chestnut Pollinizer)

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; flowers late and is valued as a good pollinizer for other French and hybrid chestnut cultivars.

directions: Belle Epine (clone CA 114) is a traditional French Castanea sativa cultivar registered under the French CTPS certification system, producing medium-sized nuts around 14 grams each with a moderate flavor. It flowers and ripens late in the season and sheds pollen at a useful time for cross-pollinating other late-blooming French and European x Japanese hybrid chestnuts, making it a valued pollinizer tree as much as a nut producer in its own right. As a straight European chestnut, it lacks the strong blight resistance of Chinese-chestnut-derived hybrids, so it is best suited to regions with lower blight pressure or grown alongside more resistant cultivars.
